newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish short day higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish short day higher.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished the holiday-shortened session on higher ground, but trade was thin and choppy during the day.

A positive tone was set early by a Washington Post story that suggested the Federal Reserve would not hike rates in February, traders said. Further strength came from the fact that the overall tone of the day's data was not strong enough to jolt bulls, sources said.
T-bond futures trade closed at 1210 CST/1810 GMT and Euros at 1200 CST and will remain closed on Monday in observance of Martin Luther King Jr Day.

The dollar and bonds were supported early by U.S. trade data that showed a smaller than expected increase in the U.S. trade deficit. The November gap rose 4.9 percent to $8.4 billion, versus an average forecast for a $9.8 billion defecit. The U.S. gap with Japan shrank 12.9 percent to $4.32 billion.
Later, most debt futures dipped into negative territory on slightly stronger than expected industrial production and capacity use figures for December.
Industrial production rose 0.8 percent, versus a forecast for up 0.6, with November revised to up 0.8 percent.
Capacity utilization was reported at 83.8 percent, compared with the 83.5 percent forecast. Use was revised to 83.4 percent in November.
Later, the University of Michigan's preliminary January consumer sentiment index at 96.0, versus 96.9 for the December final index, helped debt futures recover, traders said.
But overall the tone was lackluster as traders only modestly adjusted their positions heading into the long weekend, several traders said.

March T-bonds closed up 7/32 at 110-30/32, T-notes rose 5/32 to 108-13/32, muni-bonds ended up 8/32 at 114-20/32, T-bills rose three bps to 94.92, and June Eurodollars settled up two bps at 94.19. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
